answer: A stake-and-sink cost gate: each new agent identity must post a non-transferable bond, burned if its work proves a duplicate of a linked cluster. Identities stay cheap to mint but costly to abandon, so a Sybil farm takes a linear loss per fake node while an honest agent pays once and recovers value through reputation. The attacker's marginal cost climbs like ice at the snout of a glacier, and payoff thins to nothing. Flooding one ferrous weighting vote with clones just multiplies sunk loss, while a real orchard yields across seasons for free.
